PullRequest.Title: agentHost: use origin/main as the default branch when origin/HEAD still points at an older origin/master
PullRequest.Body:

  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

Refs #337420

When the local `origin/HEAD` still points at an old `origin/master`, Branch Changes list hundreds of unrelated files. Branch Changes in an Agents window session should compare against `origin/main`. Git sets `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` only when you clone, so it keeps pointing at `origin/master` after the remote changes its default branch to `main`. With no saved base branch, the agent host takes the session's base branch from `origin/HEAD`. Its only check is that the target ref exists, and a stale `origin/master` usually still does.

## Fix

`AgentHostGitService` now reads `origin/HEAD` through one helper, used by `getDefaultBranch`, `getDefaultBranch2` and the session git state. The helper uses the other branch instead when all of these hold:

- `origin/HEAD` points at `origin/master` or `origin/main`;
- the other of the two branches exists on `origin`;
- the target is missing or is an ancestor of the other branch.

The check runs locally, with no network calls: two `rev-parse` calls and at most one `merge-base --is-ancestor`, and only when the target is `master` or `main`. A target with commits that the other branch lacks is kept. Base branches already saved for a session are not changed, and neither is how linked worktrees choose their base.

## Not in this PR

Opening the Changes editor still creates a text model for every entry, binary files included. It drops them only after loading fails, or keeps them when binary detection misses a file. That's the other half of #337420. It needs a binary flag on the protocol's `FileEdit`, and it wouldn't help the original report, where images are stored in Git LFS and git diffs them as text.

## Repro

1. Create a repository whose `origin` has `master` at an old commit and `main` ahead of it, with 300 added PNG files.
2. Clone it while the remote's HEAD is `master`, then switch the remote's HEAD to `main` and `git fetch`. The local `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` still points at `origin/master`.
3. Check out a `vnext` branch from `origin/main` and commit a change to one file.
4. In the Agents window, start a session in that folder and open Changes with Branch selected.

Before: `301 Files`. Most are PNGs, and the Changes editor goes on to load them. After: `1 File`.

## Validation

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostGitService.integrationTest.ts` | Passed, 125 tests |
| The same, with only the source change reverted and `--grep "older origin/master"` | Failed as expected: stale and dangling targets resolve to `master` |
| `pnpm run typecheck-client` | Passed |
| `pnpm run oxlint src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostGitService.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostGitService.integrationTest.ts` | Passed |

I ran the integration tests with an empty global git config (`GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`). With my global `tag.gpgsign=true`, the existing test "name-only HEAD reads do not treat non-branch symbolic refs as branches" waits forever for a tag message, which has nothing to do with this change.

The new integration test covers three cases: a stale target (uses `main`), a diverged target (keeps `master`), and a dangling target (uses `main`).

## Evidence

I have a before/after recording (side by side, aligned by step) plus screenshots from a Code OSS dev build. They come from a `validate-ui-scenario` run of the Agents window against a standalone agent host with `--enable-mock-agent`, on the repo above. I can attach them if needed.

- **Before** (fix reverted): the session's Changes pane in Branch mode shows `301 Files`. The Changes editor renders `img-*.png` entries, some of them decoded as garbage text, and the scenario's final assertion fails.
- **After**: the pane and the Changes editor show only `guide.md` (`1 File +1 -0`), and every step passes.
- In one run each, the first Changes editor entry rendered after 1372 ms before and 200 ms after.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The helper has no result or in-flight cache; _computeSessionGitState unconditionally awaits it. File-monitor refreshes reach this path, and the state service coalesces only overlapping reads with the same directory/base/freshness key and throttles each session to five seconds. Subsequent refreshes therefore repeat the command. Exact graph traversal duration depends on history size and Git's commit-graph/disk caches.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Git child processes and commit-ancestry traversal/object reads.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For G non-coalesced directory/base refresh groups and R effective refresh rounds, distinct existing main/master tips add 2*G*R ref-resolution subprocesses plus G*R ancestry subprocesses. Within one session, queued refreshes are throttled to five seconds; overlapping reads of the same directory/base/freshness can share one read. Reachability work additionally depends on the history Git must inspect; warm filesystem/commit-graph caches do not eliminate repeated processes.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Repeated Git process creation and history traversal increase background CPU/I/O and place avoidable latency before Git-state and downstream Changes updates.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The initial default-branch probe was one symbolic-ref subprocess with no history traversal. With a saved base of main, the existing base divergence/diff stayed anchored to main, so there was no old-master traversal on this default-branch probe to offset the added work.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every effective Git-state read now performs two additional rev-parse subprocesses and, for distinct existing main/master tips, one additional ancestry subprocess. The ancestry answer is recalculated even when both immutable commit IDs are unchanged.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 125 runs merge-base --is-ancestor whenever origin/HEAD names main/master and both refs resolve to different commits; added line 1470 substitutes this helper for the previous single symbolic-ref probe in _computeSessionGitState. The configuredBaseBranch override at line 1490 occurs only after awaiting the helper, so saved bases do not avoid the new work.
Findings.Title: Reuse ancestry results across unchanged Git-state refreshes
Findings.Impact: In a long-lived clone retaining an old origin/master behind origin/main, editing files with Changes observed repeatedly launches and awaits a history reachability check, including for sessions already saved against main. This adds CPU/object-reading work and can delay Changes refreshes in large histories; distinct worktree/directory-base groups repeat it independently.
Findings.Evidence: AgentHostGitService.ts:112-125 resolves both commit IDs but does not reuse them to memoize reachability. _computeSessionGitState:1467-1471 awaits the helper before publishing state. ChangesetFileMonitorCoordinator._onRootsChanged:366-390 requests forced refreshes for watched, inactive sessions after relevant edits. AgentHostGitStateService:468-476 awaits the Git read before its refresh event; 543-546 imposes a five-second per-session throttle; 565-583 shares only in-flight directory/base reads and removes them on settlement. _runGit:1590 directly creates a child process without a shared limiter.
Findings.Recommendation: Use a bounded cache for successful ancestry answers keyed by repository and the two resolved commit IDs, and coalesce identical in-flight checks. Continue resolving refs on refresh so changed tips naturally select a new key; do not cache transient command failures.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Trusting a stale but existing origin/HEAD target selected an obsolete branch-diff base. Every unrelated changed path since that old commit became a file entry, which the Changes editor eagerly loaded before its complete document set could render.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Opening Branch Changes in an affected clone loaded potentially hundreds of unrelated files, including binaries, increasing file/model allocation and delaying editor document resolution. This consequence is established by the baseline-to-entry-to-eager-loading call path; no timing measurement is asserted.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: For a session without a saved base, a stale ancestor origin/master is replaced by origin/main before branch-diff baseline selection. Historical main-only file changes no longer enter the diff list, reducing downstream parsing, protocol payloads and eager text-model/file loading to the actual session changes. Saved bases and diverged refs remain unchanged.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: The replaced base-revision symbolic-ref probe at line 1440 supplied origin/HEAD directly to the Git-state fallback base. The new call at line 1470 and helper at 103-126 substitute origin/main when retained origin/master is its ancestor. Added integration test lines 832-856 establishes stale/diverged/dangling outcomes. AgentHostChangesetService._getBranchBaseBranch (2671-2685) uses Git-state base when none is saved; _computeBranchDiffs (1439-1440) passes it into computeSessionFileDiffs, which resolves merge-base HEAD/base and runs git diff (844-868). parseGitDiffRawNumstat (2150-2250) creates an entry for every changed path, including binary paths. _publishChangesetDiffs (2498-2519) publishes all entries. ChangesMultiDiffSourceResolver (68-75) maps each entry to a MultiDiffEditorItem, and MultiDiffEditorInput (236-246,317) eagerly resolves every side and awaits all document promises. Thus files introduced between the obsolete master tip and main caused real extra model/file loading, not merely an incorrect label.

Scenarios.Scenario: Refresh or restore Git state for observed chats, including sessions with an already saved main base
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A relevant edit or chat-availability event starts a Git-state read. The status, remote and origin-head probes must all finish before divergence/default-ref probes, state persistence and the refresh event that triggers downstream Changes updates. These background reads do not block agent execution, but do gate refreshed Changes state.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read origin/HEAD, resolve main/master commit IDs, and test ancestry; also run existing status, remote, default-ref and divergence probes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per effective directory/base read: previously one symbolic-ref for origin-head resolution; now one symbolic-ref plus two parallel rev-parse calls for a main/master target and one merge-base when both tips exist and differ. Thus G non-coalesced groups over R refresh rounds add 2GR ref probes and up to GR ancestry commands. No added work scales per changed file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The origin-head probe never traversed history. For a saved main base, existing divergence computation already used main, so the obsolete master did not add history traversal at this probe.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The complete origin-head helper is awaited by the initial Promise.all, even with a configured base. Its ancestry check can become the longest probe.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stat the working directory and run rev-parse --show-toplevel on a repository-root cache miss.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One stat/root lookup per uncached directory, with overlapping lookups shared; root/confirmed-nonrepository LRU has 100 entries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same cache, stat and root lookup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Precedes all Git-state probes on a cold root lookup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read saved base metadata and save changed Git state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Loaded records serve the saved-base read in memory; unloaded records use central state/catalog reads or a scope database fallback. Saves occur when state differs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same metadata path and save-on-change policy. Correcting a stale default can cause a one-time changed-state save, not unbounded retention.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Base resolution precedes the Git read; changed-state persistence precedes announcement.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct directory/base/freshness read groups, effective refresh rounds and commit history between main/master tips. Many chats in one directory can share an overlapping read; distinct worktrees do not share it.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: ThrottlerByKey serializes/coalesces refreshes per session and adds a five-second interval. Each effective read starts status/remote/symbolic-ref concurrently, then two rev-parse calls concurrently, then at most one ancestry command. Independent directory/base groups can run together; _runGit has no global limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Repository roots are cached/coalesced. Git-state reads are shared only while in flight, keyed by directory/base, with special forced-read sharing; entries disappear on settlement. Origin-head ancestry has neither result caching nor helper-level coalescing. Missing alternatives still incur the two rev-parse probes on subsequent reads; equal tips skip ancestry. Warm Git/disk caches do not eliminate process launches.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: unconditional awaited helper, event reachability, read-key grouping and five-second throttle are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: History size, commit-graph availability, disk cache state and number of simultaneously observed worktrees determine duration and prevalence; no measured timing is claimed.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported one medium-severity repeated-work regression: unchanged commit-pair ancestry is recalculated on recurring refreshes, including saved-base sessions that do not receive a compensating diff reduction.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open Branch Changes with no saved base in a clone retaining stale origin/master behind origin/main
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Git-state fallback base selects the diff baseline. Branch diff computation and publication precede Changes resources; opening the editor resolves all resource-side model promises before the document set is available.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve default branch, resolve HEAD/base merge-base, obtain status and run raw/numstat diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The helper adds two ref probes and at most one ancestry check per effective Git-state read. Diff remains grouped per repository, not per file. Multi-folder computation deduplicates repositories and limits repository diff jobs to five.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Default resolution used one symbolic-ref and selected the obsolete master tip. Existing diff operations then included all paths changed between that tip and HEAD.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Helper completes before the fallback base is available; merge-base/status/diff complete before publishing file entries.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Build and publish ChangesetContentChanged file entries, including binary paths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: O(D) for the effective diff-path count after repository/file deduplication. With H unrelated historical paths and C session paths, stale baseline could produce roughly H+C entries; corrected baseline produces C.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same parser/publisher, but the obsolete baseline enlarged the collection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: File list must be parsed and published before client resources are derived.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve working-file text models for every modified resource side.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One working-file model read per distinct modified URI on cold resolution. Historical additions have only a modified side, so 300 unrelated added paths imply 300 extra working-file model loads, not 600 Git blob calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing eager model resolution loaded the enlarged stale-baseline collection; the PR reduces that collection rather than changing renderer behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All document promises settle before the complete model set is installed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve original git-blob content through the agent-host resource provider, run git show and return UTF-8 content.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One content request/git show per cold distinct original-side blob URI, not per repository and not for added paths lacking an original side. Filesystem/root ownership lookups are reused where cached.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same content-read path; obsolete baseline could introduce extra original sides for unrelated edits/deletions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Original-side content is required by its model promise; those promises contribute to the editor's all-documents wait.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load the session snapshot and select saved base before Git-state fallback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per branch computation, serialized by session; loaded session state is reused. Saved bases keep precedence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same selection order, but unsaved sessions fell back to stale origin-head-derived Git state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Completes before computing the diff baseline.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Unrelated paths introduced since the old remote-default tip, actual session paths, distinct content URIs and deduplicated repositories.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Repository diff jobs are limited to five in multi-folder mode. Model resources resolve eagerly without a per-resource limiter in the input, with both sides parallel and a final Promise.all. Blob reads spawn independent git show processes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Saved-base selection is unchanged. Multi-folder fingerprints can reuse per-repository diffs. MultiDiffEditorInput caches document promises by original/modified URI pair, and root resolution is cached; cold editor opening still loads every effective file side. Binary detection occurs after model resolution and does not avoid initial attempts.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: base-to-diff-to-file-entry-to-eager-model-loading path is traced, and the added integration case proves stale ancestor selection changes to main.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual historical path count, content sizes and model cache warmth determine the benefit. The illustrative 300-path scenario is a cardinality example, not a measured benchmark.
Scenarios.Verdict: This is a concrete performance fix: corrected fallback prevents unrelated historical file loading. Recorded internally with the base-line introducing commit; did not report the removed eager-loading mechanism as a new finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: First send, worktree materialization or changing a chat's workspace
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Folder first-send resolution awaits default-branch lookup only if the base is not saved, then persists it before send can finish resolving the directory. Worktree creation awaits default-branch metadata before the repository-key creation sequencer. Workspace conversion awaits Git-state computation before publishing the new folder and allowing sends.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Default-branch/Git-state lookup, existing branch/ref/remote reads and worktree checkout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Default resolution is per unsaved-folder setup or unmaterialized worktree setup, with in-flight _getGitInfo reads shared by directory/resolve-default flag. New helper adds two ref probes and at most one ancestry command per lookup; worktree checkout remains one per newly materialized session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Default-head lookup was one symbolic-ref; branch metadata and checkout already existed. Already-materialized worktrees are still reused.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: New helper is awaited before send-directory resolution/workspace publication can proceed. Existing checkout remains a later necessary setup boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and persist base/worktree metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One saved-base check per relevant folder setup; write only when base is missing or a new worktree is recorded. Loaded base records are served in memory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same reads/writes, precedence and immediate-flush placement.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Immediate base persistence is on first-send setup path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create worktree directory hierarchy, check name collisions and perform existing include-file preparation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per new worktree, with collision checks per generated candidate; materialized sessions avoid another creation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same worktree creation and filesystem behavior; no new per-file copying is introduced by the helper.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing necessary materialization work follows default-branch resolution.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Concurrent new sessions/worktrees, unsaved folder scopes and commit histories for distinct main/master tips.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Worktree creation is sequenced per repository after default lookup. Independent setup requests can therefore overlap the new helper before entering that sequencer. Workspace catalog mutations are sequenced per session.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Saved folder bases bypass first-send default lookup; materialized worktrees are reused. _pendingGitInfo shares only overlapping same-directory requests. Root and pending branch reads are cached/coalesced, but helper ancestry is not cached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for lookup placement and added subprocess counts; existing setup work is explicitly separated from introduced work.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: One-time setup latency depends on Git process startup and ancestry cost; checkout may dominate many setups.
Scenarios.Verdict: Added setup costs are bounded per lookup and serve the stale-default correction. No separate finding beyond the shared uncached ancestry root cause.

Scenarios.Scenario: Populate branch picker or load the Mission Control project catalogue
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Picker completion awaits branches, current branch and default branch. Catalogue loading builds each project entry before publishing the catalogue/list response.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read default branch alongside existing picker branch reads, or after project root/remote reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Picker performs one default lookup per completion request, not per branch row. Catalogue performs one default lookup per distinct Git project entry. Main/master targets add two ref probes and at most one ancestry call for each effective lookup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Each lookup used one symbolic-ref plus existing verification. Picker branch enumeration and per-project remote/root reads were already present.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Default lookup participates in picker Promise.all; catalogue entry creation awaits it within the sequential project loop.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the project catalogue and canonicalize project directories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One catalogue-file read and one realpath per saved project during initial load.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same initial catalogue read and realpath validation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Precedes entry creation and list publication.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Completion requests, distinct Git projects in the catalogue and relevant commit history; not branch-row count for helper calls.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Picker's three reads run concurrently. Catalogue mutations are globally sequenced and saved project entry construction is sequential; the helper's two ref probes are parallel within each entry.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Mission Control caches _loaded and project entries, so repeated list requests do not rerun entry lookup. Existing add operations reuse known project entries. Default ancestry remains uncached when new entries or picker requests actually invoke it.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for per-request/per-project cardinality and serialized catalogue construction.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Catalogue size and history size determine aggregate cold-load delay; normal small catalogues may see little impact.
Scenarios.Verdict: No per-branch boundary fan-out. Catalogue adds bounded per-project setup work; repeated picker ancestry falls under the reported cache/repeated-work root cause.

Scenarios.Scenario: Prepare/create a pull request or merge a worktree's changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: PR context resolution sequentially awaits current Git state and default branch before preparing or creating the PR. Merge awaits Git state even though its target base is already resolved. Mutations and post-operation refresh follow.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve Git state/default branch; perform existing status, branch creation, commit, push or merge operations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: PR context calls the helper twice sequentially via getSessionGitState and getDefaultBranch: up to four added rev-parse and two added ancestry commands for unchanged tips. Creating a new branch adds another Git-state read. Merge preflight has one helper lookup; post-refresh adds one per effective grouped state read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: PR context made two inexpensive symbolic-ref probes; merge state made one. Mutation command count and ordering otherwise remain unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The repeated helper lookups are on operation preflight. Existing mutations wait for this preflight.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Push the selected branch, look up an existing PR, optionally read merge capabilities/generate metadata and create a PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One push and one existing-PR lookup per invocation; one create when no PR exists. Creation failure can cause one reconciliation lookup. Optional capability/generation requests are unchanged and do not fan out per changed file due to this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same downstream operations and reconciliation structure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Preflight finishes before these existing network steps; completion still awaits required mutations.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve saved base and persist merge/state outcomes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per operation/session, using existing metadata records and save sequencing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same metadata operations; saved targets still take precedence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Base lookup precedes preflight; outcome persistence and refresh precede completion where awaited.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Operation attempts and effective post-refresh groups; ancestry cost depends on the remote-tip pair's history, not PR file count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: PR Git-state and default-branch reads are sequential in _resolveContext. Mutations are ordered. Post-operation refresh starts source/session refreshes together, sharing only matching directory/base/freshness reads; separate keys remain independent.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No ancestry answer survives the sequential PR context calls, so overlapping-only Git-state/branch coalescing cannot remove the duplicate. Saved bases do not skip the unconditional Git-state default probe. Existing network/service caching is not changed by this diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both sequential context calls and explicit-base merge call are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Interactive cost varies with Git history/cache and network latency; network may dominate total operation time.
Scenarios.Verdict: Corroborates the reported unchanged-tip repeated ancestry mechanism; no separate network regression or correctness-only finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Capture repository-info telemetry at agent turn begin/end
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Capture awaits Git state/status, remote identity, baseline/safety checks, snapshots, content-exclusion results and patches. Turn event handling starts this capture without awaiting it, so it is background work rather than an agent-response prerequisite.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read Git state plus existing untracked/status, safety, snapshot, diff and patch commands.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One helper lookup per actual begin/end capture, with an additional default lookup only if all base fallbacks are absent. New helper adds two ref probes and at most one ancestry command per lookup. Existing patch work is one command per allowed descriptor, capped by 100 changed files and four concurrent patches; rename paths are deduplicated within the descriptor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Git-state default probe was one symbolic-ref. Existing safety checks, file-count gates and patch limiter were already present.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: New helper gates telemetry capture's later steps, not model/agent progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check content exclusion through the SDK RPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One batched request for deduplicated old/new paths of eligible descriptors, not per file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same batched content-exclusion RPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background capture awaits it before scheduling patch extraction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create/copy/stage temporary-index snapshots when the working tree is changed, then clean them up.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing snapshot operation at capture and stable-tree recheck; clean HEAD-equivalent working trees avoid temporary-index work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same clean-tree fast path, temp-index setup and cleanup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required within background telemetry capture.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize eligible relative paths and capped/truncated patch descriptors and submit repository telemetry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most 100 changed-file descriptors before content-exclusion filtering, with existing payload-size gates. Begin result is deduplicated by telemetry message ID and end removes its stored result.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same caps, serialization, begin/end lifecycle and reporting.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off agent-response critical path; reporting is invoked without awaiting its returned work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Eligible agent turns and their actual begin/end captures; relevant remote-tip history. Existing descriptor work is bounded to 100 changed files and fewer than 30 baseline commits.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Begin/end lifecycle is ordered per message. Git-state/untracked reads initially run in parallel; patches use a four-job limiter. Independent turns can capture concurrently without a new global helper limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Begin capture is shared per telemetry message ID; end is conditional on begin result and clears the entry. Repository-root lookups are cached. Ancestry results are not reused across captures, but no new retained telemetry state is added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for added helper invocation and background scheduling; existing bounded patch/RPC behavior is directly inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Telemetry enablement, eligible turn frequency and history determine background overhead; no claim that it blocks response startup.
Scenarios.Verdict: Background recurrence reinforces the same reported ancestry-cache issue. Existing per-descriptor patches, JSON allocation and SDK reads are not newly introduced and were not reported.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the distinct performance-review pass over the full two-file inventory and every diff page. Submitted one high-confidence medium-severity finding for uncached repeated ancestry checks, with effective read grouping and throttling accounted for. Recorded the stale-baseline/eager-file-loading fix with base-line blame provenance. Checked startup/setup, live refresh, Branch Changes, picker/catalogue, PR/merge and background telemetry scenarios; omitted correctness-only concerns and unchanged optimization opportunities. Static read-only analysis; exact durations and prevalence remain unmeasured.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
